questions.q: What is a SEQUENCE in SQL Server?
options: A type of index used for sorting
A special kind of column, like IDENTITY
A standalone database object that generates numbers, not tied to any one table or column
A built-in system table
questions.explain: Unlike IDENTITY, a SEQUENCE exists as its own object, independent of any specific table.

questions.q: What does NEXT VALUE FOR do?
options: Returns the sequence's starting value every time it's called
Deletes the sequence object
Returns the next number in the sequence and marks it used
Resets the sequence back to its START WITH value
questions.explain: Each call hands out the next number — e.g. 1, then 2, then 3 — and that value won't be handed out again.

questions.q: How can a SEQUENCE be shared in a way an IDENTITY column cannot?
options: A SEQUENCE can only be used by exactly one row
The same SEQUENCE can be used by multiple different tables
A SEQUENCE can only be read by administrators
IDENTITY columns can also be shared across tables, so there's no real difference
questions.explain: An IDENTITY column is locked to one table and column; a SEQUENCE is a standalone object several tables can draw from.

questions.q: What real advantage does a SEQUENCE have over IDENTITY when you need the key value for related inserts?
options: IDENTITY values can be read before any insert, just like a SEQUENCE
A SEQUENCE never requires a data type
A SEQUENCE automatically inserts related rows for you
You can call NEXT VALUE FOR and get the number BEFORE inserting anything
questions.explain: With IDENTITY you must insert first and then read SCOPE_IDENTITY(); with SEQUENCE you can get the value up front.

questions.q: In 'CREATE SEQUENCE dbo.LessonSeq START WITH 1 INCREMENT BY 1;', what does INCREMENT BY 1 control?
options: How much the sequence's value goes up by each time NEXT VALUE FOR is called
Whether the sequence can be shared across tables
The first value the sequence will ever hand out
How many rows the sequence can generate in total
questions.explain: START WITH sets the first value; INCREMENT BY sets the step size for every subsequent NEXT VALUE FOR call.
